items.title: Show HN: Proc-CLI – An agent-friendly CLI tool for process and port management
items.desc: title: proc description: Semantic CLI tool for process management. Target by port, PID, name or path. [Skip to content](main) Target processes by port, PID, name or path. proc is a semantic CLI tool for process management on macOS, Linux and Windows. Find what's on a port, why it's there, and stop it, in one command you'd guess on the first try. \~❯proc kill :3000 Ends whatever is listening on port 3000 immediately (SIGKILL). Asks first, and dryrun previews. A leading colon means a port: proc acts on whatever is listening on it. Command onwhyforbyinlistinfoportstreeorphansstuckkillstopfreefreezethawunstickwatchwait Target :3000 Ends whatever is listening on port 3000 immediately (SIGKILL). Asks first, and dryrun previews. A leading colon means a port: proc acts on whatever is listening on it. 1234 Ends process 1234 immediately, and nothing else. A number is a PID: that one process and nothing else. node Ends every node process, after listing them and asking. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. :3000,:8080,node Ends all of them in one go, after one confirmation. Commas combine targets. A process matched twice is only acted on once. node in . Ends only this folder's node processes, not your editor's or another project's. in keeps any target inside a folder and the folders below it. Most commands take it. :3000 Shows what's listening on port 3000: its name, PID, folder, CPU, memory and how long it has been running. A leading colon means a port: proc acts on whatever is listening on it. 1234 Works the other way too: shows process 1234 and every port it listens on. A number is a PID: that one process and nothing else. node Shows each node process and the ports it listens on. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. :3000,:8080,node Answers all three at once: what's on ports 3000 and 8080, and which ports the node processes hold. Commas combine targets. A process matched twice is only acted on once. node in . Shows only the node processes started in this folder, and their ports. in keeps any target inside a folder and the folders below it. Most commands take it. :3000 Traces what's on port 3000 back through its parent processes, so you see what started it: a terminal tab, a tmux session, your editor. A leading colon means a port: proc acts on whatever is listening on it. 1234 Shows the chain of parents that led to process 1234, with how long each one has been running. A number is a PID: that one process and nothing else. node Traces every node process back to whatever started it. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. :3000,:8080 Traces what holds ports 3000 and 8080, one chain each. Commas combine targets. A process matched twice is only acted on once. ./server.py Finds the processes running server.py from this folder. With proc for, the target is a file: relative, absolute or starting with ~. ./logs/app.log Finds whatever has app.log open, such as a server that's still writing to it. With proc for, the target is a file: relative, absolute or starting with ~. node Lists every process whose name or command line matches node. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. node in . The same, limited to processes started in this folder. in keeps any target inside a folder and the folders below it. Most commands take it. . Lists everything started in this folder or below it. With proc in, the target is a folder. . is the one you're in. \~/code/shop Lists everything started in ~/code/shop, wherever you run it from, even after the folder has been deleted. With proc in, the target is a folder. . is the one you're in. no target Lists every process, busiest first. No target: proc looks at every process. node Lists only the processes matching node. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. \status zombie Lists zombie processes: ones that have exited but haven't been cleaned up by their parent. Flags narrow any listing. status takes running, sleeping, stopped or zombie. 1234 Shows everything about process 1234: folder, path, user, parent, status, CPU, memory and uptime. A number is a PID: that one process and nothing else. :3000 Shows everything about whatever is listening on port 3000. A leading colon means a port: proc acts on whatever is listening on it. node Shows the full details of each node process. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. no target Lists every listening port and the process behind it. No target: proc looks at every listening port. \exposed Only the ports other machines can reach, the ones worth checking. exposed keeps ports listening on 0.0.0.0 or ::, and local the localhost ones. \in . Only the ports held by processes started in this folder. in keeps any target inside a folder and the folders below it. Most commands take it. no target Shows every process as a tree of parents and children. No target: proc looks at every process. node Shows each node process with the processes it started. Anything else is a name, matched against each process's name and full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. 1234 ancestors Goes up instead of down: from process 1234 to the first process the system started. A number is a PID. ancestors turns the tree upside down. no target Finds processes whose parent has exited, like dev servers left behind by a closed terminal. System services are left out. items.author: yazeedaloyoun
items.descZh: proc 是一款适用于 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的语义化命令行工具，专为进程管理设计，允许用户通过端口、PID、进程名或文件路径快速定位和操作进程。其核心功能包括查找进程详情、终止进程、追踪进程树以及管理端口占用，支持单命令完成复杂操作。亮点在于直观的语法设计，例如使用冒号前缀表示端口目标，数字代表 PID，名称匹配支持模糊查找，逗号可组合多个目标，而 "in" 关键字能限定操作范围至特定目录，同时提供 dryrun 预览和确认提示以确保安全。该工具特别适合开发者在处理端口冲突、停止遗留服务或分析进程依赖关系时使用，能显著提升故障排查和日常维护的效率。
items.quote: 前导冒号表示端口：proc 作用于正在侦听的任何内容。
items.titleZh: Show HN：Proc-CLI – 用于进程和端口管理的代理友好的 CLI 工具

items.descZh: 这篇文章介绍了一个交互式图表工具，旨在可视化犹太教、基督教、伊斯兰教、印度教和佛教这五大宗教在9000年间的演变历程，背景源于对宗教历史脉络的系统梳理需求。核心功能是将这些宗教整合到一个家族树中，通过时间线展示它们的分支和发展，每个节点都链接到详细章节以提供引用来源。亮点包括具体性能数字，如覆盖9000年时间跨度、包含180个有日期的首次事件和86个分支，确保了数据的可追溯性和学术严谨性。该工具适用于宗教研究者、历史教育工作者或对宗教演化感兴趣的公众，可用于教学、自学或深度探索宗教历史。
items.quote: 印度教、佛教、基督教、伊斯兰教、犹太教置于一棵家族树上：包含180个标注日期的节点和86个分支，每个节点和分支都链接到引用它的章节。
items.titleZh: Show HN：宗教是如何演变的？图表、地图、引文

items.title: Show HN: Nodecode, open-source living agent in Lisp that rewrites itself for you
items.desc: Hi HN, we're Mike and Thom. Agents of the future should only have one tool (the interpreter, ideally a LISP eval), nothing more or less; to interact with the world. Agents remember by writing markdown files. NODECODE remembers by rewriting itself. And that is in itself a new paradigm in working
items.author: svsairevanth
items.descZh:
这篇文章分享了一种关于未来 AI Agent 设计的激进理念。作者认为，理想的 Agent 应该只配备一个工具，即一个 LISP 解释器，通过它来与世界交互。在记忆机制上，他们提出 Agent 通过写 Markdown 文件来记忆，而 NODECODE 则通过重写自身来记忆，这构成了一种全新的工作范式。

核心功能是构建一个极简但强大的 Agent，其交互能力源于一个纯粹的解释器，记忆和进化则通过外部文件或自我代码重写实现。亮点在于将“自我重写”作为记忆和进化的核心机制，这代表了一种从外部工具依赖转向内部能力构建的范式转变。适用场景是下一代 AI Agent 的架构设计与开发。
items.quote: 未来的 Agent 应该只拥有一个工具（一个解释器，理想情况下是 LISP eval），不多不少，仅此而已，用以与世界交互。
items.titleZh: Show HN：Nodecode，Lisp 中的开源实时代理，可以为您重写自身

items.title: Show HN: Drint – packaging dielines and 3D box mockups as an MCP server
items.desc: description: Use Drint inside an AI assistant’s chat: find mockups, get dielines at an exact size, open your own projects in 3D. title: Connect Drint to Muse, Claude and ChatGPT — Help centre Drint image: https://drint.io/home/shareen.jpg [Skip to content](main) [Help centre](/help) › AI assistants Connect Drint to Muse, Claude and ChatGPT Use Drint inside an AI assistant’s chat: find mockups, get dielines at an exact size, open your own projects in 3D. One address for every assistant Drint is an MCP server — the standard way AI assistants plug in other apps. Muse, Claude and ChatGPT all connect to the same address: https://drint.io/mcp. Finding mockups and listing dieline structures work straight away, without an account. When the assistant needs your account (your projects, dieline files), it sends you to drint.io to sign in and click Allow. Meta Muse 1. If Drint is listed in Muse’s Settings → Connectors, turn it on there. 2. If it is not, send Muse one message: “Connect to the Drint MCP server at https://drint.io/mcp”. Muse sets up the connection, tests the tools and keeps it for next time. 3. When asked, sign in to Drint and click Allow. 4. In Muse’s settings, choose whether Muse may run Drint’s tools on its own or asks you first each time. Claude 1. In Claude (web or desktop app), open Customize → Connectors and search for Drint — or click Add custom connector. 2. Name it Drint, paste https://drint.io/mcp as the URL and click Add. 3. Click Connect, sign in to Drint and click Allow. 4. In a chat, turn Drint on in the tools menu and ask, for example: “find a kraft paper bag mockup and show it in 3D”. Claude Code Run claude mcp add transport http drint https://drint.io/mcp, then type /mcp in Claude Code to sign in to Drint. ChatGPT 1. In ChatGPT’s settings, open the apps section (Apps & Connectors) and turn on Developer mode under the advanced settings. 2. Create a new app named Drint with the address https://drint.io/mcp and OAuth signin. 3. Sign in to Drint and click Allow. 4. In a chat, pick Drint and ask. Mockups and projects open in Drint’s own 3D viewer inside the chat — rotate, recolour and resize them there. No account needed search_mockups — finds ready 3D mockups: boxes, bags, bottles, labels, apparel… open_mockup — opens one in 3D. list_dielines — the dieline structures Drint draws, with their default sizes. With your Drint account get_dieline — a PDF / AI or SVG dieline at an exact size, from a FEFCO or ECMA code or a Drint type. Free has 3 a month. make_dieline — PDF / AI, DXF and CF2 files for the diemaker. DXF and CF2 need Pro. Both dieline tools count on your plan like a download in the app. list_my_projects, open_my_project — your own projects, opened in 3D (with the watermark grid on Free, as in the app). review_inbox — your Review inbox: work handed on to 3D Studio or Drint AI and the results waiting for you. send_to_3d_studio — a link that opens the project with Continue already open; click Build a scene in 3D Studio to send it. my_drint — your plan and what is left. View only, and removing a connection On drint.io’s Allow page, tick View only if the assistant should only look at your projects and Review inbox: it makes no dieline files and uses nothing on your plan. Each connection works in one space you pick on the same page — your own, or a print shop’s. See and remove connected assistants in Account → Signin & security → Connected apps. Changing your password removes all of them. The assistant never sees your password, and no Drint tool deletes anything or takes a payment. Still stuck? items.descZh: Drint作为一个包装设计软件，现已通过MCP服务器标准集成到Muse、Claude和ChatGPT等AI助手中。其核心功能允许用户在聊天界面中直接搜索3D模型、获取精确尺寸的dieline文件，并打开个人项目进行3D可视化。亮点包括免费用户每月可获取3个dieline文件，而Pro版本提供高级功能如生成DXF和CF2文件。工具内置的3D查看器支持模型的旋转、重新着色和调整大小，无需额外软件。适用于设计师和包装工程师在AI环境中快速原型设计和协作，提升工作效率。

items.descZh: GOD是一个开源的实时控制室平台，专为智能体社会设计，让使用者能够像上帝一样掌控由智能体组成的虚拟城镇。核心功能包括暂停时间、与智能体灵魂低语、干预下一步行动以及一键重置整个世界，所有操作均可通过单一点击完成。项目亮点在于无需安装、无需API密钥，提供浏览器即时回放功能，并支持本地快速部署，降低了使用门槛。该平台适用于多智能体系统研究、AI行为调试、实时监控及仿真场景，帮助开发者直观观察和操控复杂智能体交互。通过实时控制与可视化，GOD为智能体社会的研究与教学提供了强有力的实验工具。
items.quote: 像神一样俯瞰一座智能体小镇。暂停时间。对灵魂低语。扭曲下一步。重置世界——这一切，只需轻轻一点。

This choice is separate from website analytics. Allow adsNo thanks[Privacy policy](/privacy/) FIND YOUR NEXT SMALL CHALLENGE Daily games for a little time well spent Choose a quick test of knowledge or a story you can shape. Little Fun Games currently has three browser games: Krillion, our independent trivia edition; The Bonding Trial, an unofficial Fourth Wing fan adventure; and Pooplestyle wordladder practice. Different moods, different worlds, and no account to create. For a different pace, our [Skate 3 in browser guide](/inbrowser/skate3/) introduces an external fan project and explains its gameresource requirements before you launch. Which game fits your break? A daily challenge has a clear stopping point: finish today’s set and come back for the next one. Repeatable modes suit a longer break. Our story adventure works differently again, with choices and discoveries instead of a knowledge score. Pick the experience you want before you start. Game or mode What you do Choose it for [Krillion Daily](/krillion/) Answer seven questions per UTC date A small daily ritual [Krillion Classic](/krillion/) Try seven shuffled prompts Another short round [Krillion Unlimited](/krillionunlimited/) Keep answering while you have lives A longer trivia challenge [The Bonding Trial](/fourthwinggame/) Make nine story choices A dragonrider adventure [Poople practice](/poople/) Change one letter at a time An untimed word ladder Daily and classic trivia both mix three Standard, three Advanced and one Specialist category. Our practice library has 70 categories and 730 accepted answers. The daily schedule rotates categories over ten days, while classic and unlimited sessions shuffle the library. Unlimited means you can keep playing; it does not mean every question will be new forever. Start playing in your browser 1. Choose a game above. The coral play button opens today’s trivia. The dragonrider card opens the story adventure. The lilac Poople section opens a word ladder. All three work without an installation. 2. Set your pace. Trivia normally gives you 25 seconds per question. Turn on relaxed play before starting if you prefer to think without a clock. The story adventure lets you read and choose at your own pace. 3. Play one step at a time. In trivia, type one answer that fits the category. In the adventure, read the situation and choose how your rider responds. In the word ladder, change one letter and press Enter. None of these games needs a controller. 4. Explore your result. Read the trivia explanations or discover your dragon bond. You can stop there, try another mode, or follow a different story path. In a trivia round, an accepted answer ends the question and an unrecognised entry lets you try again while time remains. After feedback appears, use “Next question” or press Enter to continue. The answer list and extra reading are there when you want them, so you can choose between a quick game and a slower learning break. Daily trivia: familiar answers count too Our trivia game asks you to name one member of a set. Read the boundary carefully: a country is not a continent, and a Canadian territory is not a province. An answer that fits the question is more useful than an unusual answer outside the set. Accepted answers earn 10, 30, 60 or 100 points from editorial familiarity tiers. These are gamedesign choices, not measurements of real players’ answer frequency. The game checks answers and awards points automatically; you never have to grade yourself. Capitalisation, spacing, punctuation and accents are normalised, with support for selected aliases and small, unambiguous typos. Editorial points are awarded automatically after an accepted answer. The feedback includes a short explanation and a source. If an answer appears to be missing, “This answer should count” opens an editable email draft to our team. A suggestion is reviewed before any question data changes. Explore three different worlds Krillion turns a score into an underwater dive.
